Subject: Question re: 'Derivative Use' carve-out in your DPA

Hi Priya,

We're reviewing the DPA draft you sent (v4). Legal flagged Section 4.2, the 'Derivative Use' prohibition, and asked whether Redwood would consider a scoped exception for model debugging and telemetry-based improvements that never persist training weights. They want narrow, timeboxed rights for troubleshooting (e.g., to improve prompt routing and safety filters) but no model tuning that could incorporate customer PII.

Two asks from Meditronics:
- Can you confirm whether "derivative use" in your DPA includes ephemeral runtime signals used for immediate inference improvements?
- If you will not allow any exceptions, can you provide operational evidence (audit log paths, retention periods) showing how telemetry is isolated from model training?

We'd like to get an answer this week if possible so procurement can finish the security review.

Thanks,
Carlos Ruiz
Head of Cloud Security
Meditronics

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Ben (AM) and Marissa (Legal) to propose an approach. High level: Redwood's standard DPA prohibits using customer content to train any base models for product-wide improvements, but there are limited telemetry and debug exceptions that are:
- scoped to customer-specific logs and never used for cross-customer model tuning,
- timeboxed (retention window configurable), and
- subject to engineering controls and audit logs.

Ben — can you confirm the commercial trade we can offer (e.g., a 90-day telemetry window + SOC2 evidence) and whether we should offer a special exception in the DPA as a redline?

Marissa — can you propose a tight-definition of "Derivative Use" and a short redline that would allow ephemeral telemetry for debugging but explicitly exclude training or model weight updates? Carlos, we'll send a proposed clause for your review later today.

Best,

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@meditronics.com>, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question re: 'Derivative Use' carve-out in your DPA

Carlos — thanks for surfacing. Attached is a proposed narrow redline for Section 4.2 ("Derivative Use"). Key points:
- Define 'Derivative Use' as "the use of Customer Data to update or modify model parameters or to train or fine-tune foundation models".
- Add an explicit carve-out: "Customer-Scoped Operational Telemetry" which is described as ephemeral request/response logs, anonymized prompt traces, and aggregated performance metrics used solely for (i) per-customer debugging, (ii) safety monitoring for the customer's instance, and (iii) routing optimizations that do not alter shared model weights.
- Operational constraints: 30-day default retention, maximum 90 days only by written agreement; telemetry must be stored in a customer-segregated bucket; any use for training requires a separate executed amendment.

I've attached the redline doc and a short tech appendix describing how telemetry is kept out of model training (KV cache separation, separate pipelines). Karthik, please confirm the technical accuracy and whether the appendix is sufficient evidence for their auditors.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_Derivative_Definition_20270603.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@meditronics.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question re: 'Derivative Use' carve-out in your DPA

Quick technical confirmation: the language Marissa proposed maps to our implementation. Additional clarifications:
- "Anonymized prompt traces" means prompt tokens are hashed and only feature-level metadata (latency, error codes, token counts) are retained in the telemetry stream used for routing.
- Training pipelines are isolated: telemetry ingestion writes to 'telemetry-<acct>' and we have an explicit policy that prevents telemetry buckets from being included in training snapshots. That's enforced via deployment guards and a weekly audit.
- Audit artifacts (S3 paths, retention policies, weekly audit digest) can be shared under an NDA or via SOC2 reports.

From an engineering perspective, the carve-out is safe provided we keep the 'no-training' requirement and a documented access control list. Happy to jump on a call if Carlos wants to walk through the pipeline.

-Karthik
Staff Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
